 DharmaNexus strongly corroborates these connections: its Pali text-reuse alignments show that the bulk of the *Mucalinda Sutta* (§1.3–6.4) is virtually identical to the *Mahākhandhaka* narrative (Kd 1, §3.1.1–3.4.8), shares identical verse segments with the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 2.8, §4.1–6.4), and shares opening stock phrasing with the *Bodhi Suttas* (Ud 1.1–1.3) [DharmaNexus; Anandajoti 2010]. Across languages, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with Sanskrit biographical cycles in the *Saṅghabhedavastu*, the *Catuṣpariṣatsūtra*, and the *Lalitavistara*, as well as the Tibetan *Abhiniṣkramaṇa-sūtra* (D0301) [DharmaNexus], confirming the widespread transmission of the Mucalinda narrative across northern and southern Buddhist textual traditions [Allon, The Senior Manuscripts; Nakamura, Gotama Buddha].
